chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, who said:

A man came to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and said: 'I was a slave owned by a group of people, and I married a free woman without the permission of my masters. Then they emancipated me after that. Should I renew my marriage with her when I was emancipated?' He (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Did they know that you had married a woman while you were their slave?' He said: 'Yes, and they were silent regarding me and did not reproach me.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Their silence from you after their knowledge is an acknowledgment from them. Remain upon your first marriage.'
ai.seo_question: Does a slave need to renew his marriage contract after being freed by his masters?
ai.summary: In this ruling from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that the masters' silence, following their knowledge of the slave's marriage, serves as implicit consent (iqar), thereby validating the existing contract upon emancipation. This principle highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on tacit approval in commercial and familial transactions, distinguishing it from cases where explicit permission is strictly required. It underscores the flexibility within Islamic family law to preserve marital stability when the master's rights are not actively infringed upon.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Muawiya Bin Wahab who said,

‘A man came over to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so he said, ‘I was an owned slave of a group of people, and I married a free woman without a permission of my master. Then he emancipated me after that. Do I have to renew my marriage with her when I was emancipated’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘Did they know that you had married a woman and you are an owned slave of theirs?’ So he said, ‘Yes, and they were silent from me, and they did not fault upon me’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Their silence from you after their knowledge is an acceptance from them. You are affirmed upon your first marriage’.
